title: Composition of quasi-affine morphisms
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that both $f$ and $g$ are quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]: the inverse image of every affine open of the target is a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Then $g\circ f:X\to Z$ is quasi-affine in the same sense. No finite-type, Noetherian or separatedness hypothesis on the schemes is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01SN, morphisms.tex, lemma-composition-quasi-affine, statement and proof, lines 2280--2316. Used to extend charts from an affine open of the original base without losing relative quasi-affineness.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U\subseteq Z$ and put $W=g^{-1}(U)$ and $E=f^{-1}(W)$. By [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], $W$ is quasi-affine. The definition also says that every affine-open preimage under $f$ is quasi-compact, so $f$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding], $W$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and has an open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow V=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. Hence $E$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open]. The affine scheme $V$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), applied to $j$, shows that $j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

The restriction $f_W:E\to W$ is quasi-affine: an affine open $B\subseteq W$ is also an affine open of $Y$, and $f_W^{-1}(B)=f^{-1}(B)$ is quasi-affine by the hypothesis on $f$ and [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. Apply [lem-trf-quasi-affine-relative-spec-embedding] to $f_W$. It gives a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_W$-algebra $\mathcal A$, a relative spectrum $R=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_W(\mathcal A)$, and a quasi-compact open immersion $i:E\hookrightarrow R$ over $W$.

Set $\mathcal A'=j_*\mathcal A$, with its $\mathcal O_V$-algebra structure induced by $\mathcal O_V\to j_*\mathcal O_W$. Its underlying module is the ordinary direct image of the underlying module of $\mathcal A$. Since $j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] makes that module quasi-coherent. Thus $\mathcal A'$ is a quasi-coherent algebra in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec]. By clause (2) of that node, $T=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_V(\mathcal A')$ exists and is affine, taking the affine open to be all of $V$.

Identify $W$ with its open image in $V$. For every open $B\subseteq W$, the definition of direct image gives $(j_*\mathcal A)|_W(B)=\mathcal A(j^{-1}(j(B)))=\mathcal A(B)$, with identical restriction maps, multiplication and structure-algebra action. Hence $\mathcal A'|_W\cong\mathcal A$ as $\mathcal O_W$-algebras. Clauses (3) and (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] identify $R$ with the open subscheme $T_W=\pi^{-1}(W)$ of $T$, where $\pi:T\to V$ is the structure morphism. The inclusion $T_W\hookrightarrow T$ is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion].

The open immersion $i:E\hookrightarrow R=T_W$, followed by the inclusion $T_W\hookrightarrow T$, identifies $E$ with an open subscheme of the affine scheme $T$: its image is open in the open subset $T_W$, hence open in $T$, and both structure sheaf maps are restriction isomorphisms [def-weil-open-immersion]. Step 1 proved $E$ quasi-compact. Thus $(g\circ f)^{-1}(U)=E$ is isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Since $U$ was arbitrary, [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism] gives the conclusion.
